title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 64
paragraphs: After this the Lacedaemonians equipped a larger expedition and sent it against Athens, appointing as commander of the army their king Cleomenes son of Anaxandrides, and sending it this time not by sea but by land. With these, when they had invaded the land of Attica, the Thessalian cavalry first engaged in battle; and in no long time they were routed—more than forty of their men fell, and the survivors departed without more ado and went straight back to Thessaly. Cleomenes then came to the city together with those Athenians who wished to be free, and began to besiege the tyrants shut up in the Pelasgian wall.
